name: MCP OAuth authorization for a single protected resource
summary: Bounded OAuth 2.1 authorization server and bearer verification for one MCP resource with public PKCE clients; the product owns login, consent and ownership policy.
use_when: A product exposes an MCP server over HTTP and remote MCP clients must obtain user-authorized bearer tokens using the MCP authorization flow.
The authorization server, the protected MCP resource and the consent UI run in the same product and the issuer URL is fixed configuration.
non_goals: OpenID Connect, identity provider federation or a universal user model
Replacing the MCP protocol implementation; the official SDK serves tools
Confidential clients, client secrets, implicit, device or client-credentials grants
Remote client metadata (CIMD, jwks_uri or client_uri fetches) in the first slice
Browser authentication, session management, consent page rendering and CSRF protection for the consent form
Rate limiting, abuse detection and durable storage backends beyond the reference adapter
proposed_guarantees: Authorization code grant for public clients with PKCE S256 only, plus rotating refresh tokens; plain PKCE and other grants are rejected

Exact redirect URI matching against registered URIs; HTTPS by default, numeric loopback HTTP and exact localhost HTTP with an explicit valid port available as separate opt-ins; no custom schemes or localhost subdomains
Redirect URI and client are validated before any redirect; earlier failures answer 400 directly and never redirect
RFC 8707 resource binding: authorization and token requests carrying a different resource are rejected and verification rejects tokens for any other resource
RFC 7591 dynamic client registration for public clients only, with bounded input, no client secret and no fetch of client-supplied URLs
RFC 8414 and RFC 9728 metadata derived from a fixed configured issuer, never from request Host headers
Scopes are bounded by a configured ceiling; requests may narrow it and approvals may narrow the request but never widen it
Consent records and authorization codes are single use and consumed atomically; a code is burned on any subsequent mismatch
Access tokens are opaque random secrets stored only as SHA-256 digests with mandatory expiry; revocation is checked on every verification
Verification fails closed on storage error, unknown, revoked, expired or resource-mismatched tokens
Approval requires an application-supplied subject and binding so the product can enforce live ownership on every request
Refresh tokens rotate atomically, never extend the absolute grant lifetime, and reuse by the bound client revokes the whole token family; verification checks grant revocation on every request
failure_modes: Product skips live subject or resource ownership checks after verification and serves another tenant's data
Product consent form lacks CSRF protection or an authenticated session, allowing forged approvals
Issuer or resource misconfiguration mismatches the deployed URL and clients cannot complete the flow
Loopback redirects enabled on a deployment that should not admit local clients
Storage unavailable or corrupt: authorization, token issuance and verification fail closed
Already admitted work may finish after revocation
Open dynamic registration without rate limiting permits client record exhaustion
Reference durable adapter is single process and not for distributed or multi-host storage
A lost committed refresh response or concurrent refresh by two client instances causes reuse revocation and requires reauthorization; no grace window

evidence.basis: Contract derived from an existing maintainer implementation serving MCP clients in one product; its source, revision and identifying details are not published and readers cannot verify it. No AMSL consumer adoption is claimed.

The MCP authorization specification requires OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, protected resource metadata, authorization server metadata, resource indicators and supports dynamic client registration; this defines the interoperability boundary the contract targets.
Candidate implementation and security regression tests are available at an immutable revision; automated tests and review are not a human approval or independent audit.

Serenity candidate consumes the pinned library and includes SQLite lifecycle, browser consent and native-client qualification evidence. Local native probes are reported evidence, not production adoption; repository tests are reproducible.

alternatives.name: Official MCP Go SDK auth and oauthex packages
alternatives.assessment: Provides resource-side bearer verification hooks, protected resource metadata and client-side OAuth primitives. It does not provide an authorization server with consent, registration, code issuance or token storage; reuse it for the MCP server and resource metadata.

alternatives.name: golang.org/x/oauth2
alternatives.assessment: Client library only; no authorization server behavior.

alternatives.name: go-oauth2/oauth2
alternatives.assessment: General-purpose authorization server supporting many grants, confidential clients and refresh tokens. Reviewers should confirm whether a fail-closed, fixed-issuer, single-resource, public-client-only profile is easier to obtain by configuring it than by this contract.

alternatives.name: ory/fosite
alternatives.assessment: Comprehensive OAuth 2 and OpenID Connect framework with PKCE and resource indicators. Broad surface and configuration burden; a bounded MCP profile may still be justified, which the review must decide.

open_questions: Candidate implementation is pinned and public CI passes; security API maintainer review and release approval remain pending.
Serenity consumer integration is in PR #271 with local native-client evidence and reproducible regression tests; public consumer CI is pending and no merged production adoption is claimed.
Human maintainer review of the security API is pending; AI review does not count. Retain CANDIDATE.
Reviewers must decide whether go-oauth2/oauth2 or ory/fosite configured to this profile would make the AMSL implementation unjustified.
Remote client metadata remains excluded; adding URL fetching requires a revised contract and SSRF review.
Consent CSRF, login and ownership policy remain product responsibilities; the contract should state the minimal product obligations a consumer must test.
